column2: 中古英语 wolf ← 古英语 wulf ← 原始西日耳曼语 *wulf ← 原始日耳曼语 *wulfaz ← 原始印欧语 *wĺ̥kʷos（狼）
column3: a wild animal of the dog family that hunts in packs
column5: A wolf howled somewhere up the valley.|Wolves hunt in packs through the winter.
column6: a wild dog-like animal that hunts as one of a pack – 犬类的野兽，成群一起猎食
column7: 狼：那种野兽本身|野狼：强调它未经驯养这一点

column2: 中古英语 womman ← 更早的 wifman ← 古英语 wīfmann（女性之人），由 wīf（女子）＋ mann（人）复合而成
column3: an adult female person
column5: A woman in a red coat asked the way.|The scheme helps women returning to work.
column6: a grown female person – 成年的女性
column7: 女人：日常说法|妇女：偏正式，多用于统称

column2: 中古英语 wonder ← 古英语 wundor（奇事、奇迹）← 原始西日耳曼语 *wundr ← 原始日耳曼语 *wundrą
column3: a feeling of surprise mixed with admiration, or to want to know
column5: She gazed up in wonder at the dome.|I wonder whether he ever knew.
column6: struck by something one cannot account for – 遇上说不清的事，一时呆住
column7: 惊奇：见所未见而心生讶异|想知道：因不明其故而心里打转|奇迹：能引起这种感觉的那件事

column2: 中古英语 wonderful ← 古英语 wundorful，即 wonder ＋ 形容词后缀 -ful
column3: extremely good, causing delight
column5: We had a wonderful time in Wales.|She has a wonderful voice.
column6: good enough to leave one marvelling – 好到让人赞叹不已
column7: 极好的：程度上好得出众|令人赞叹的：好到旁人不由称奇

column2: 中古英语 wode ← 古英语 wudu（木、林）← 原始西日耳曼语 *widu ← 原始日耳曼语 *widuz ← 原始印欧语 *h₁weydʰh₁-（分开）
column3: the hard material that trees are made of, or a small forest
column5: The table is made of solid wood.|They walked through the wood at dusk.
column6: the hard stuff a tree is made of, and the place trees stand – 树的那种硬质材料，以及树成片长着的地方
column7: 木头：从树上取下的那种材料|木材：加工备用的那些木头|树林：树成片生长的那片地

column2: 由 wood ＋ 后缀 -en（由…制成）构成，1530 年代始见；逐步取代了旧词 treen
column3: made of wood, or stiff and without feeling
column5: A wooden gate closed off the lane.|His acting was stiff and wooden.
column6: made of wood, or as unbending as wood – 用木头做的，或硬得像木头一样不会转
column7: 木制的：材质是木头|呆板的：举止或表情硬得不活络

column2: 中古英语 wolle ← 古英语 wull ← 原始西日耳曼语 *wullu ← 原始日耳曼语 *wullō ← 原始印欧语 *h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂（羊毛）
column3: the soft thick hair of sheep, or thread made from it
column5: The blanket is pure wool.|She knitted the scarf from grey wool.
column6: the soft curly hair sheep grow, spun into thread – 羊身上那层软卷的毛，可纺成线
column7: 羊毛：剪下来的那种纤维|毛线：把它纺成的那种线

column2: 中古英语 word ← 古英语 word ← 原始日耳曼语 *wurdą ← 原始印欧语 *werdʰom（言），出自 *werh₁-（说）；与 verb 同源
column3: a single unit of language, or a short statement
column5: Look the word up in the dictionary.|He gave me his word.
column6: the smallest piece of speech that stands on its own – 语言里能独立站住的最小一块
column7: 词：语言的那个单位|话：说出来的一段内容|诺言：一句算数的话，故以「话」代指承诺

column2: 中古英语 werk ← 古英语 weorc ← 原始西日耳曼语 *werk ← 原始日耳曼语 *werką ← 原始印欧语 *werǵ-（做）
column3: effort spent to get something done, or something produced
column5: He goes to work by bus.|The clock no longer works.
column6: effort put in so that something gets done – 使出力气，让事情做成
column7: 工作：为谋生或达成目标所做的事|作品：做出来的那件成果|运转：机器起作用、能动这一层

column2: 中古英语 worchere，即 work ＋ 施事后缀 -er；取代了旧词 wright（← 古英语 wyrhta）
column3: a person who does a job, especially manual work
column5: The workers voted to accept the offer.|Two workers were repairing the roof.
column6: one who does the work with their own hands – 亲手把活做出来的那个人
column7: 工人：以体力劳动为业的人|劳动者：泛指从事劳动的人

column2: 由 work ＋ shop 复合而成；shop 一支 ← 古英语 sceoppa（棚、摊）
column3: a room where things are made or repaired, or a short practical course
column5: He keeps his tools in the workshop.|She ran a two-day writing workshop.
column6: a place fitted out for making and mending – 备好家伙、供人动手做与修的那个场所
column7: 车间：工厂里分区作业的那间|工作间：个人动手做活的小屋|研习班：一群人动手练习的短期课程

column2: 中古英语 world ← 古英语 weorold ← 原始日耳曼语 *weraldiz（人的世代、人世），由 wer（人）＋ eld（年岁）合成；取代了外来词 mounde
column3: the earth and all the people on it, or a particular sphere of life
column5: News of it travelled round the world.|She is known in the world of dance.
column6: the whole span of human life and where it goes on – 人世的全部范围及其所在
column7: 世界：地球及其上的一切|世上：人所处的这个范围|界：某一领域内的那个圈子

column2: 由 world ＋ -wide（遍及…的）构成；world 一支 ← 古英语 weorold（人世）
column3: happening or existing everywhere in the world
column5: The company has worldwide operations.|The song became a worldwide hit.
column6: reaching every part of the earth – 触及地球上每一处
column7: 全球的：范围覆盖整个地球|世界范围的：说得更具体，指遍及各国

column2: 中古英语 worm ← 古英语 wyrm ← 原始西日耳曼语 *wurmi ← 原始日耳曼语 *wurmiz（虫、蛇）← 原始印欧语 *wr̥mis（虫），或出自 *wer-（转）
column3: a small soft creature with a long thin body and no legs
column5: A worm wriggled out of the wet soil.|Birds pull worms from the lawn.
column6: a long soft legless creature that moves by bending – 又长又软、没有腿、靠身体屈伸移动的小动物
column7: 虫：这类小动物的通称|蚯蚓：钻土的那一种，最常见

column2: 中古英语 worien（掐、勒）← 古英语 wyrġan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *wurgijan ← 原始印欧语 *werǵʰ-（缠、挤）；本义是勒紧，后转为心里发紧
column3: to feel anxious, or to make someone anxious
column5: She worries about her son's health.|The delay worried everyone involved.
column6: a tightness in the mind that will not let go – 心里被揪住，松不开
column7: 担心：心里挂着可能出的坏事|发愁：担心到成了负担|使不安：把这份紧张加到别人身上

column2: 中古英语 worse ← 古英语 wiersa ← 原始西日耳曼语 *wirsiʀō ← 原始日耳曼语 *wirsizô，是「坏」的比较级
column3: of lower quality or in a more serious condition than something else
column5: The second draft was worse than the first.|His cough got worse overnight.
column6: further down the scale than the thing compared with – 比拿来比的那个更往下
column7: 更差的：质量或表现不如另一个|更严重的：情况恶化，程度加深

column2: 中古英语 worschippe ← 古英语 weorþsċiepe，即 worth（值、尊）＋ -ship
column3: the act of showing deep respect to a god, or to do so
column5: They gathered for morning worship.|He worships at the chapel on the hill.
column6: treating something as worthy of the highest honour – 把某个对象当作最该受敬的来对待
column7: 崇拜：心怀极度敬仰|礼拜：按仪式向神致敬这件事

column2: 中古英语 worste ← 古英语 wierrest ← 原始日耳曼语 *wirsistaz，是 *ubilaz（坏）的最高级
column3: of the lowest quality or most serious kind
column5: That was the worst meal of the trip.|Prepare for the worst outcome.
column6: the one furthest down the scale, with none below – 落在最下的那个，再往下没有了
column7: 最差的：质量或表现排在末位|最糟的：情况坏到不能再坏

column2: 中古英语 worth ← 古英语 weorþ ← 原始西日耳曼语 *werþ ← 原始日耳曼语 *werþaz（有价值的）← 原始印欧语 *wert-
column3: having a particular value, or good enough to justify the effort
column5: The house is worth twice what they paid.|It is worth asking before you go.
column6: measuring up to what is given for it – 与为它付出的相称
column7: 值…的：折算下来相当于某个价|值得的：所得抵得过所费|价值：那份可折算的分量

column2: 由 worth（值得的）＋ while（一段时间）复合而成，字面「值得花那段时间」
column3: good enough to be worth the time or effort spent
column5: The extra training proved worthwhile.|It is a worthwhile cause to support.
column6: repaying the time it takes – 花掉的时间能换回来
column7: 值得做的：所费的工夫抵得过所得|有意义的：做了有价值，不算白费

column2: 中古英语 worthy ← 古英语 *weorþiġ，即 worth ＋ 形容词后缀 -y
column3: deserving respect or a particular treatment
column5: The scheme is worthy of support.|He proved a worthy opponent.
column6: measuring up to what is being given – 够得上所给的那份待遇
column7: 配得上的：担得起某种对待或称号|可敬的：品行使人愿意敬重

column2: 名词 ← 中古英语 wund ← 古英语 wund ← 原始西日耳曼语 *wundu ← 原始日耳曼语 *wundō（伤）← 原始印欧语 *wen-（争、搏）
column3: an injury where the skin is cut or broken
column5: The wound took three weeks to heal.|Two soldiers were wounded in the raid.
column6: a place where the body has been cut open – 身体被划开的那一处
column7: 创伤：皮肉破开的那处损伤|使受伤：造成这样的损伤这个动作

column2: 中古英语 wrappen（裹、折），更早词源不明；或与原始印欧语 *werp-（转、绕）相关
column3: to cover something by folding material round it
column5: She wrapped the gift in brown paper.|Wrap the wire round the post twice.
column6: folding material round something until it is covered – 把料绕着它折过来，直到盖住
column7: 包裹：用纸布把物件裹起来|缠绕：绕着某物一圈圈缠上|披巾：披在肩上裹住身体的那件

column2: 中古英语 wreth ← 古英语 wriþa（圈、环）← 原始日耳曼语 *wriþô ← *wrīþaną（拧、编）← 原始印欧语 *wreyt-（拧）
column3: a ring of leaves or flowers, used as decoration or in mourning
column5: A wreath of holly hung on the door.|They laid a wreath at the memorial.
column6: leaves or flowers twisted into a closed ring – 把枝叶或花拧编成一个闭合的圈
column7: 花环：装饰用的那种圈|花圈：吊祭时献上的那种

column2: 中古英语 wrek ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 wrek ← 古诺尔斯语 *wrek ← 原始日耳曼语 *wrekaną（追赶）← 原始印欧语 *wreg-（追、猎）
column3: what is left of something badly damaged, or to destroy it
column5: Divers explored the wreck on the seabed.|The storm wrecked half the orchard.
column6: what remains after something has been broken up – 被彻底毁坏之后剩下的那些
column7: 残骸：毁坏后留下的那堆东西|毁掉：把某物彻底破坏这个动作

column2: 中古英语 wrench ← 古英语 wrenċ ← 原始日耳曼语 *wrankiz ← 原始印欧语 *wreng-（转）
column3: a tool for turning nuts, or to pull with a sudden twist
column5: He tightened the bolt with a wrench.|She wrenched the door open.
column6: a sudden hard twist, and the tool that gives one – 猛地一扭，以及施出这一扭的工具
column7: 扳手：卡住螺母转动的那件工具|猛扭：突然用力拧转这个动作

column2: 中古英语 wrecched ← wrecche（可怜的、流落的）← 古英语 wrecca（流亡者）← 原始印欧语 *wreg-（驱赶）
column3: very unhappy or in very poor condition
column5: They lived in wretched conditions.|He felt wretched about the whole affair.
column6: in so poor a state as to be pitied – 境况差到让人可怜
column7: 凄惨的：处境或遭遇令人不忍|糟糕的：状况或感受很坏

column2: 中古英语 wrinkle ← 动词 wrynklen ← 古英语 *wrinclian（起皱）；与荷兰语 wrinkel 同族
column3: a small line or fold in skin or cloth
column5: Fine wrinkles showed round her eyes.|Iron out the wrinkles in the shirt.
column6: a small fold left where a surface has been pressed together – 表面被挤到一处后留下的小折
column7: 皱纹：皮肤上那些细线|褶皱：布料等被挤压后起的折

column2: 中古英语 wrist ← 古英语 wrist ← 原始西日耳曼语 *wristu ← 原始日耳曼语 *wristuz ← *wrīþaną（拧、转）；与 writhe 同支
column3: the joint between the hand and the arm
column5: He wears a watch on his left wrist.|She sprained her wrist playing tennis.
column6: the joint that lets the hand turn on the arm – 让手能在臂上转动的那个关节
column7: 腕部：手与臂相接的那一段|腕：单字说法，多用于复合词

column2: 古英语 writan ← 原始日耳曼语 *writaną（刻、划）← 原始印欧语 *wrey-（撕、划）；本义是刻划，后转指书写
column3: to form letters or words on a surface
column5: She wrote her name at the top.|He writes for a local newspaper.
column6: leaving marks that stand for words – 留下能代表话语的那些痕迹
column7: 写：用笔留下字迹|书写：同义，偏书面
